newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end lower despite new economic planners.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end lower despite new economic planners.

text.p: Stocks closed lower on Wednesday despite the naming of new economic ministers as foreign selling on bank shares provoked a chill toward the close.

Brokers said hopes of an economic recovery with a new economic team waned rapidly due to investor jitters on weak market fundamentals. President Kim Young-sam appointed a new finance minister, Kang Kyong-shik, a ruling New Korea Party lawmaker with extensive experience in government.
"The choice of Kang as a new finance minister has been widely known. Now a slowing economy is a more pressing concern," said a Daishin Securities broker.
The composite stock index closed 5.07 points lower at 674.90. Earlier it reached a high of 684.55.
Brokers said foreigners sold more than one million bank shares, including 400,000 shares of Commercial Bank of Korea and 200,000 shares of Cho Hung Bank.
"Scepticism about the nation's banking industry was growing among foreign investors," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon securities.
President Kim also named Lim Chang-yuel to replace Ahn Kwang-koo as trade minister. A total of seven ministerial portfolios changed hands today in a cabinet reshuffle.
Brokers earlier said sentment improved in anticipation that the new economic team would expand the foreign stock ownership limit soon and push a deregulation drive.
Trading volume totalled 38.77 million shares, compared with 28.06 million on Tuesday.
Hyundai Motor lost 400 won to 23,500 after releasing figures showing a fall in February car sales.

Hyundai Motor, South Korea's largest carmaker, said its vehicle sales in the month fell to 82,471 units from 87,244 a year earlier. Hyundai said an economic slowdown was largely to blame for the fall.
